item.title: Using energy at home
item.description: Learn how to describe equipment, heating and daily energy use in a home. Practice words for reading a display and turning devices on or off.

children.definition: The number shown or recorded on a device that measures how much of a service you have used.
children.example: Take a photo of the meter reading before you move out.

children.definition: To connect equipment to an electricity supply by putting its plug into a socket.
children.example: I need to plug in the lamp before I can turn it on.

children.definition: To disconnect equipment by taking its plug out of a socket.
children.example: I unplug the fan when I put it away for winter.

children.definition: A row of electrical sockets that share one cable and plug.
children.example: The phone chargers are plugged into a power strip under the desk.
collocations: a power strip under the desk

children.definition: To stop a device or the lights from working by using a control.
children.example: Please switch off the hall light when you leave.

children.definition: A point in a wall or on a device where you connect an electrical plug.
children.example: Is there a socket near the kitchen table?

children.definition: Designed to use less energy than an ordinary product doing the same job.
children.example: We put an energy-saving bulb in the desk lamp.

children.definition: A low-power state in which equipment stays ready to work again quickly.
children.example: The screen is on standby, so it wakes when I move the mouse.

children.definition: The amount of electrical energy used over a given time.
children.example: The chart shows our electricity use in each month of the year.

children.definition: A digital device that records how much energy you use and can send the information automatically.
children.example: The smart meter sends our electricity readings to the supplier.

children.definition: Material that helps keep heat from passing into or out of a place.
children.example: The new insulation helps the upstairs rooms stay warm for longer.

children.definition: A machine used for a job in the home, such as washing clothes or keeping food cold.
children.example: The washing machine is the only appliance running right now.

children.definition: A control that sets when the heating will start or stop.
children.example: We set the heating timer to turn the heat on before we get up.

children.definition: A device that gives out heat to warm the air in a room.
children.example: The radiator near the window keeps the bedroom warm.
